title: The Standards Check & Part 3 Marking
whatItIs: Part 3 and the standards check are marked the same way: 17 competences in 3 areas, each scored 0 to 3, for a total out of 51.

keyFacts.text: You MUST take a standards check when DVSA asks, even if you have no car or aren't working as an ADI.

keyFacts: Usually every 4 years; you may be called sooner because of your pupils' driving test results.
About 45 minutes, with the pupil driving for about 40 minutes.
Fail 3 standards checks and you're removed from the ADI register and must retake the ADI tests.

keyFacts.text: When giving lessons you MUST display your ADI registration at the passenger-side edge of the windscreen.

rows: Fail: you won't join the register
Grade B: you can join the register
Grade B: you stay on the register
Grade A: high standard of instruction
Grade A: high standard of instruction
notes: Each competence: 0 no evidence · 1 a few elements · 2 most elements · 3 all elements.
Automatic fail: 7 or less in risk management, or the examiner stops the lesson for danger.

a.label: Part 3
points: Bring a pupil, a car and trainee licence (or licence or passport)

b.label: Standards check
points: For qualified ADIs, usually every 4 years; free
Bring a pupil, a suitable car and your ADI certificate

onTheTest.question: An ADI scores 42 on a standards check, with 9 in risk management. What's the result?
onTheTest.why: GOV.UK standards check: 31 to 42 is grade B; grade A starts at 43. The automatic fail applies only at 7 or less in risk management.

onTheTest.question: On part 3 and the standards check, what does a score of 2 for a competence mean?
options: A few elements of competence shown
onTheTest.why: Examiner guidance 3.12 and 4.10: 0 = no evidence, 1 = a few elements, 2 = most elements, 3 = all elements. A 2 is acceptable with clear areas to improve.

traps: 30 is still a fail: grade B starts at 31.
A high total can't save you: 7 or less in risk management is an automatic fail.
Your pupil can't be an ADI or someone preparing for their own part 3.
You can complain about how the check was run, but you can't appeal the examiner's decision.
